chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sayf ibn Amira and Salama Sahib al-Sabiri, from Abu Usama Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that
the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) freed a thousand owned slaves from the toil of his own hands.

key_terms.أَعْتَق: Freed, emancipated; the act of manumission in Islamic law (itq)
key_terms.كَدّ يَده: Toil of one's hand; earnings from manual labor, emphasizing personal effort rather than inherited or gifted wealth
key_terms.مَمْلُوك: Owned slave; a person held in bondage as property

ai.seo_question: How many slaves did Imam Ali free and how did he earn money to free them?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a sound chain from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), reports that Imam Ali (AS) emancipated one thousand slaves — purchasing them entirely with the earnings of his own manual labor. This extraordinary act of piety demonstrated Imam Ali's personal commitment to the liberation of the enslaved, setting an example that surpassed mere legal obligation. In the context of early Islamic society, where slavery was a pervasive institution, the freeing of a thousand slaves represented an immense wealth dedicated entirely to the cause of human freedom.
